- Model consistently underestimates true prices, especially in the early part of the 30-day forecast horizon.
- Forecasts show a strong upward bias in the first 5–10 days, then gradually flatten or slightly decline — but true prices often rise sharply after the initial spike.
- After a price spike (e.g., 70+), model tends to overcorrect or plateau, while true prices often continue rising or show volatility.
- Model fails to capture mean reversion in the short term — true prices frequently revert to lower levels after a spike, but model holds higher values.
- Forecasts are too smooth; true prices exhibit more volatility, especially in the middle to late period (days 15–30).
- Model underestimates the magnitude of price increases following a low point (e.g., after 60–65), often missing the “rebound” phase.
- Forecasts show a lag in responding to recent price spikes — true prices often rise faster than model predicts.
- Model tends to overestimate the “bottom” of a price cycle and underestimate the “top” — especially in the last 5–10 days of the forecast.
